subtype: Team hit by a late finisher [Receiver]
passage: At the NGO's Thursday review, Divyansh looked at the clock: 4:40. The grant report was due to the funder at nine the next morning, and it still lacked the beneficiary table that Saurabh had promised on Tuesday, then Wednesday. Divyansh had written every other section on time and now sat with a blank page and a folded-up plan. The table arrived at 6:15 in the evening with two columns missing. Divyansh phoned home to say dinner would be late again, ordered a cup of tea from the corner stall and began compressing three hours of checks into one. By 10 pm the report was finished, but tired hands had made three small mistakes that only showed the next day.

qa.q: At what time did the beneficiary table arrive?
qa.a: The table arrived at 6:15 in the evening with two columns missing.

qa.q: What was Divyansh feeling while phoning home to say dinner would be late?
qa.a: Divyansh was tired and frustrated, and worried about the deadline, since the late table meant staying on to compensate.

qa.q: What could Divyansh do next time when waiting for someone else's input?
qa.a: Ask Saurabh early for a firm date and a partial version, and warn the team when the date looks unsafe, so the report can be planned around it.

qa.q: How might Saurabh see the delay?
qa.a: Saurabh may not realise the cost to Divyansh, treating it as the table's own lateness, when in fact it fell on the person waiting.

grounding: A person waiting for someone else's late input compresses their own work and stays late to compensate.

passage:
Subject: Friday's report and the late file

Dear Kamal,

I wanted to tell you plainly how Thursday looked from my side. Your figures came at 6:40 pm, and the client presentation was at nine the next morning. I had two hours of proofreading planned and ended up rebuilding the charts until 1 a.m. I'm not writing to blame you; I know the figures were tangled. But I was tired and a bit anxious on Friday, and I made a mistake on slide six. Could we agree that if a date looks shaky, you tell me the day before, and send whatever part you have? I can work with half a table. I can't work with none, late.

Thanks,
Asif

qa.q: At what time did Kamal's figures arrive on Thursday?
How does Asif feel about writing to Kamal?
qa.a: Asif feels careful and a little uneasy, wanting to explain without blaming, and states plainly that Friday was tiring and anxious.

qa.q: What does Asif ask Kamal to do in future?
qa.a: Asif asks Kamal to say the day before if a date looks shaky, and to send whatever part is ready.

qa.q: How might Kamal feel on reading the email?
qa.a: Kamal may feel a little embarrassed or defensive at first, but the calm tone and the clear request may make it easier to agree.

grounding: A person waiting on a late input rebuilds work overnight and explains the effect in a calm message.
